title: Ficciones

description.main: Ficciones collects anonymous found photographs of 1970s–80s China that Sun Yanchu sourced from antique markets and altered by hand with collage, drawing, gold leaf, and paint, obscuring and reinventing the images' original narratives. Published by Jiazazhi Press in 2016 as a hardcover, spiral-bound edition of 500, it won the inaugural Gucang Dummy Book Award, selected by Martin Parr, in 2015.
description.extended:
Ficciones is Chinese artist Sun Yanchu's altered-photograph project, which won the inaugural Gucang Dummy Book Award, selected by Martin Parr, in 2015.

The book gathers anonymous photographs Sun found in antique markets across China: snapshots of family gatherings, travel, and daily life from the 1970s and 1980s. Working directly on the found prints with collage, drawing, gold leaf, and paint, he obscures faces and layers in fragments of contemporary news, blurring the line between the photographs' original documentary content and his own invented narratives. Published by Jiazazhi Press in Ningbo in August 2016, the book is hardcover and spiral-bound, 112 pages, 18 × 23 × 3 cm, in a first edition of 500 copies, with text in Chinese and English.

Sun Yanchu (b. 1978, Zhoukou, Henan Province) lives and works in Zhengzhou, working by hand on found and self-made photographs. His awards include the Lianzhou International Photo Festival New Photography Award (2011) and the Jinan International Photo Biennale Best Photographer Award (2012); a related series, Developer Paintings, applies darkroom chemistry and brushwork directly to photographic paper. Ficciones followed Obsessed, Sun's 2011 debut with Jiazazhi Press.
description.artist_bio: Sun Yanchu (b. 1978, Zhoukou, Henan Province) lives and works in Zhengzhou. He won the MIO Photo Award (Morimura Yasumasa) Special Award in 2010, the Lianzhou International Photo Festival New Photography Award in 2011, and the Jinan International Photo Biennale Best Photographer Award in 2012. His later series, Developer Paintings (2013–18), uses darkroom chemicals and brushwork applied directly to photographic paper. He is represented by M97 Gallery, Shanghai.
